title: An Empirical Analysis of Racial Categories in the Algorithmic Fairness Literature
findings: The paper's findings are not about religion. Religion is mentioned only in passing as an example of a 'protected attribute' under U.S. anti-discrimination law and as a 'sensitive attribute' in the computer science literature, often listed alongside race, gender, and sexual orientation. The core analysis and findings are focused exclusively on the inconsistent and often unjustified ways racial categories are defined and used in the algorithmic fairness literature.

measurement_description: The paper does not conduct a benchmark measurement related to faith or religion. It performs a content analysis of academic papers on algorithmic fairness to understand how they conceptualize and operationalize *racial* categories. Religion is occasionally mentioned as an illustrative example of another legally protected or 'sensitive' attribute, analogous to race, but it is not a subject of the paper's analysis.
